root_causes.description: The payment service is the faulted component: an injected http_abort fault causes payment server requests to be aborted, matching the incident signature 'payment-http_abort-seed42'. Because payment is a leaf called directly by checkout, the aborts surface at checkout as a downstream dependency failure rather than within payment's own aggregated series.

evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate should spike above 0 (baseline < 0.01) when http_abort is injected on payment
http_abort should yield error-status traces containing a payment span

evidence.expected_baseline: payment is a leaf service invoked directly by checkout

root_causes.description: checkout directly depends on payment, so aborted payment calls would cause checkout's PlaceOrder path to fail as a downstream dependency failure, propagating errors to the frontend.

evidence.expected_baseline: payment is a direct checkout dependency on the order path

root_causes.description: frontend is the user-facing entry point (load-generator → frontend → checkout); failure of checkout because of the payment http_abort would surface at frontend as failed checkout/order requests.

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.000 p50=0.000 p95=0.000 p99=0.000 max=0.000 | no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend error_rate should rise if checkout fails on the purchase path

evidence.observed_value: frontend → checkout, recommendation, product-catalog, cart, shipping, currency, ad
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend is the entry point upstream of checkout

remediation_steps: Disable the payment http_abort fault-injection feature flag in flagd and confirm the flag state propagates to the payment service.
Restart/recycle the payment deployment pods to clear any in-flight aborted requests and stale fault state.
Verify recovery: payment server error_rate returns to ~0 and checkout/frontend error_rate and order success rate return to baseline.
Add a synthetic check on the checkout→payment call path to alert on payment abort errors before they propagate to frontend.
If the abort originates from the external payment provider rather than the injected flag, validate provider credentials, timeouts and circuit-breaker configuration.
